subject: tech
title: Point, Click, Drag
about: Getting around a screen: the pointer follows the mouse or a finger on the trackpad, a click chooses and a double-click opens, a tap is a click on a touch screen, drag means press, hold and move, plus scrolling and the mouse wheel, spreading and pinching to zoom, swiping, a long press and the right mouse button for more choices, the back arrow, and which action fits which job. NC K2-CS-03 (operate software to perform tasks) and K2-CS-02 (hardware parts and what they do). Read it together with a mouse or his tablet in reach so he can try each move as it comes up.
tip: Say the action and let him do it on the real tablet or mouse: tap, drag, swipe, pinch, long press, back.

cards.q: You slide the mouse to the right. Which way does the pointer on the screen go?
cards.note: The pointer copies the mouse. Slide right and it goes right, slide up and it goes up.

cards.q: You slide one finger up the trackpad on a laptop. Which way does the pointer move?
cards.note: A trackpad is a mouse you rub. One finger slides the pointer, and a tap on the pad is a click.

cards.q: You press the mouse button once and let go. What is that called?
cards.note: A click is one quick press. Put the pointer on a thing and click to choose it.

cards.q: You click two times very fast on a folder. What happens to the folder?
cards.note: Two fast clicks open a folder or a file on a computer with a mouse. On a tablet, one tap opens.

cards.q: On a tablet there is no mouse. What is the same as a click?
cards.note: One gentle tap with a finger does what a click does: it chooses or opens.

cards.q: You press on a picture, hold, and move it across the screen. What is that called?
cards.note: Drag means press, hold and move, then let go. It carries things to a new spot.

cards.q: You drag a picture to a new spot. How do you put it down there?
cards.note: Lift your finger or let go of the button. The picture stays where you dropped it.

cards.q: You want to draw a line in a drawing app. Which action do you use?
cards.note: Press where the line starts and drag to where it ends. The line follows your finger.

cards.q: The page is too long to see all at once. How do you see the rest?
cards.note: Scroll means slide the page up or down. On a tablet slide one finger, and on a computer roll the wheel.

cards.q: What does the little wheel on top of a mouse do?
cards.note: Roll the wheel toward you and the page slides down. Roll it away and the page slides up.

cards.q: You put two fingers on a photo and spread them apart. What happens to the photo?
cards.note: Spreading two fingers zooms in. The photo grows so you can see the little things.

cards.q: You pinch two fingers together on a big photo. What happens to the photo?
cards.note: Pinching zooms out. The photo shrinks back so you can see all of it.

cards.q: You slide your finger fast across the screen to see the next photo. What is that called?
cards.note: A swipe is a quick slide. Swipe left or right for the next picture or page.

cards.q: You hold your finger on an icon and little choices pop up. What did you do?
cards.note: A long press is a tap that stays. It shows extra choices, like move or delete.

cards.q: A mouse has two buttons. What does the right button do?
cards.note: The left button clicks and chooses. The right button opens a little list of extra choices.

cards.q: You opened the wrong page. Which arrow takes you back to the page before?
cards.note: The back arrow points left. It takes you to the page you were on before.

cards.q: You want to move a photo into a folder. Which action do you use?
cards.note: Drag carries things. Press on the photo, hold, slide it onto the folder, let go.

cards.q: You want to see the next page of a story on a tablet. Which action do you use?
cards.note: Swipe from right to left like turning a page. Swipe back to go to the page before.
